Preface

This book presents artificial intelligence and machine learning framework for renewable energy systems. The machine learning models with respect to solar energy storage system predictions are analyzed in Chapter 1. The fourth component of the Internet of things (IoT) system is the user interface; this helps the users to control IoT. Chapter 2 highlights the study and implementation of various types of fuzzy structures using rule-based interfaces for steady-state and transient analysis. Chapter 3 provides a survey of the role, impact, and challenges, and recommended solutions of IoT for smart buildings. Chapter 4 presents a comprehensive design of a low-cost smart single-phase energy meter monitoring system. Chapter 5 explains the IoT-based smart grid. Chapter 6 presents maximum power point tracking control using particle swarm optimization algorithm for photovoltaic (PV) panel affected by partial shading due to shadow casting. Partial shading casted on a PV panel will produce multiple peaks’ power characteristic curve, thus tracking the global peak becomes a challenge especially under dynamic changing partial shading condition. Chapter 7 discusses a wireless system for monitoring and controlling of an electrical substation using NodeMCU (Wi-Fi module), Arduino Uno (microcontroller), ThingSpeak server, and Blynk. The different parameters of the substation such as current, voltage, power factor, frequency, and temperature are monitored using various sensors and electronic components. Smart grid–based big data analytics using machine learning and artificial intelligence has been discussed in Chapter 8. Chapter 9 presents the IoT-based intelligent solar energy-harvesting technique with improved efficiency.

1 Artificial intelligence and Internet of things for renewable energy systems

Abstract

The sustainability incredibly insists in having innovations in renewable energy. To obtain an unsullied and a well-grounded environment, innovations in the present mechanisms have to be uplifted ensuring a predictive framework and an enormous outcome can be expected. The goal needs to be met to establish new research concepts and to move on the energy requirements in optimization of the existing machine learning (ML) framework. With the lot more renewable energy existing in nature, the two most variable and commonly used renewable energies are solar and wind. Its cons are nonuniformity of power and its dependency on external environmental factors. Due to this, sole dependence on renewable energy is not possible, and hence conventional power grid is also to be considered when any sort of predictive analysis needs to be done. Hence, more concentration is to be made on forecasting of renewable energy and on smart grids ensuring continuous equilibrium and balance within renewable energy and conventional grid. The electricity demand and supply of power can be predicted using ML algorithms ensuring better savings with operational costs. The two-way electricity and information flow will prove smart grid in future ensuring continuous monitoring of the network bringing more requirements for ML framework. The early warning systems incorporated by Germany symbolize a very good example of how ML algorithms analyze the real-time data from various renewable energy sources to analyze the total amount of energy requirement of the country. Google invention on DeepMind proves that the energy efficiency is 3.5 times more compared to the energy demands of the last 5 years. The innovations on intelligent home energy management systems prove promising energy usage with ML in real time. The consumer or the customer behavior can be predicted easily with intelligent techniques along with various other features like weather or climate modeling ensuring a complete and interoperable framework that suits the conventional grids. Artificial intelligence helps in sustainability of the grid with more focus on demand response. The energy management and operation cost management in smart grid is a promising feature incorporating ML algorithms in renewable energy. The optimization on managing the asset along with its maintenance ensures efficient management of power. The large amount of data collected brings data mining and prediction, thereby enabling more analytics on data. To establish such a kind of platform, various transfer models for solar and wind need to be applied along with irradiance to power models incorporating blending of information along with its categorization in ML algorithms. Feature selection methods along with the diversified algorithms in ML for diversified applications ensure continuous upgradation in framework rather than integrated approach.

Keywords: renewable energy, artificial intelligence, machine learning framework,

1.1 Solar energy storage systems and grid-connected PV systems

To consider being an infinite feature, renewable energy is significantly acquired from natural resources. Since the natural resources are capable of providing renewable energy endlessly, it can be utilized infinitely. Regardless of any vulnerable pollutant’s emission, the renewable energy can be harnessed, which are considered as a significant feature. Renewable energy generation sources are very essential for providing green energy to remote rural areas as well as urban areas. Some of the renewable energy resources are solar power, wind power, biomass, ocean wave energy, geothermal energy, hydroelectric power, and tidal power. Renewable energy source is often termed as alternative energy resources, since it is considered being a replacement to fossil fuels and nuclear power. There are a few aspects of renewable energy as follows:

  • Existence of renewable energy is perpetual, and it is infinite in the environment.

  • Always able to be harnessed, unlimitedly.

  • Known being a clean alternative energy than fossil fuels.

  • Can be replenished consistently.

1.1.1 Overview of solar energy system

Solar energy is one amid massively available renewable energy source and best cleanest energy source. Solar energy’s key source is sun’s radiation obtained from the Sun. Solar-powered electrical generation depends on photovoltaic (PV) and heat engines. The solar energy usage is always anticipated to proliferation around the world in the forthcoming centuries. Mainly, middle and low latitudes might be the chief energy source which improves economy after global and local crises. Solar energy is pollution free and comparatively no greenhouse gases are emitted. Solar technologies are generally characterized by two methods: (i) passive solar and (ii) active solar. Both the technologies mainly rely on capture, convert and distribution of sunlight thereby enabling solar energy. These active solar techniques use solar panels and thermal collectors to harness the energy. Building orientation to the Sun is considered as a passive solar technique. Solar power is one amid best sunlight conversion processes into electricity, either in a straight line through PV or through concentrated solar power (CSP) method. A CSP method tracks the Sun for huge area focusing.

In solar energy supply, energy storage plays a pivotal role. A technology that preserves the energy as well as transforms it into electricity for supplying it according to the power demand of end-user is called energy storage system. Accordingly, if produced power exceeds the required level, the surplus energy can be preserved in order to be utilized at high demand. Based on the large size storage integration, the conventional power grid is designed and the idea of balancing between generation and demand, almost 40% of solar off-grid systems lifetime costs or even more might be attributed to the storage. The solar energy availability at any point on the Earth varies with year, with day and night, and with the weather conditions. So do electrical loads which might be covered by supply systems based on solar energy. Even though the utilization of energy storage is immensely inevitable in a power system, and direct electrical energy storage besides distributed small-scale storage is of wide range in off-grid applications, yet they are considered being insignificant in most of the electricity industries.

In grids, the increasing PV penetrations lead to high demand of energy storage and new opportunities with regard to distributed direct storage, since they are highly necessitated in the industry sector. In terms of new opportunities, optimal managing end user greatly desires patterns as well as aggregated network flows, enhancing end user reliability in addition to power quality, sharing system components balance amid PV, as well as storage equipment are predominantly considered. Distributed electrical energy generated from large-scale to small local production is guaranteed through solar–thermal concentration and PV plants. In power sector, there exist a few challenges of balancing the power generation and requirement with suffering from supply constraints and shortages in power, since the electricity demand is constantly increasing every day. The transformation from conventional sources to nonconventional sources is crucially necessitated with regard to balancing the ratio of power production and demand. The core objective of utilizing solar as energy is the augmentation of power production as well as energy dependability expansion based on social, ecological, independent, and financial beneficial properties. To balance the differing time patterns of loads and solar energy production, an energy storage must be included in almost all stand-alone energy supply systems. For resolving the electrification issues in areas where the grid is not available, solar PV-based stand-alone systems become a potential solution [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. However, the following design challenges remain in this system, that is, (1) maximum power extraction from PV array; (2) preventing battery from overcharge and over discharge; (3) conversion from dc to ac; and (4) facility for sufficient voltage boosting. As a widespread renewable energy sources, PV solar system is highly utilized by the countries with tropical climate that are situated around equatorial area [6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14].

The movement of the Sun in a day, weather, and passing clouds greatly impacts over the production of solar energy and the solar PV’s output power [15, 16]. Though there are various benefits, like reduction of greenhouse emission, use of fossil fuel reduction in electricity and extemporizing energy independence quantity [17] is contributed by high penetration rate of PV generation systems, yet it may cause reverse power flow to grid and high network losses in grid generation because of high-generation power supplied at the time of low demand. In recent days, the significance of PV systems becomes lesser in electric infrastructure, besides their impact over entire quality and dependability of grid power turns out to be insignificant. However, for obtaining the emission reduction, enhanced infrastructure dependability, and energy independence, the state and federal endeavor for augmenting the PV systems penetration over local and regional utility grids.

But still PV generation possibly begins to adopt the significant negative impacts across overall grid, if PV penetration touches the maximum levels, that is, 5–20% of overall generation. In the context of high-level PV penetration, on utility operations and load side equipment, a wreak havoc may occur by this intermittency due to fluctuations in grid voltage and power factor. Generally, in accordance with the energy capacity, the storage systems are rated (i.e., watt-hours) that rely on the application which utilized the storage. 1.1.1.1 High-energy storage requirement in PV systems

In the perspective of technology and economy, the electricity utility companies face numerous difficulties due to the integration of high-penetration PV system, transmission, and distribution network. In output, both magnitude and change rate are considered being significant, the system might switch from full output to fundamentally zero.

The high-level PV penetration impacts are reduced to some extent due to PV’s distributed feature: on the grid, the intermittent generation effects over large regions will be as minimal. However, the worst-case possibilities need to be addressed by the utilities. For guaranteeing the balance of sufficient voltage and power quality, the area regulation is highly necessitated at the time of high transients. In case of low PV generation, convergence of energy demand is validated through some kind of backup generation. Besides, distributed PV generation quantity fetched online increases spinning reserve amount requirement, since most utilities necessitate “spinning reserve,” which is generally equal to power output produced [18]. The requirement for further spinning reserve/storage for intermittent PV generation backs up at a high penetration level. For accommodating a high PV penetration and further distributed besides the generation of electricity sources intermittently, such as enhanced flexibility, improving various load management, storage technologies integration, and even restricted curtailment for extreme events, the utility grid needs to be evolved entirely, in many ways. For defining the next-generation grid infrastructure that consists of aforementioned areas, there are lot of endeavors have been taken. On the basis of current grid and high-penetration PV, a contemporary work termed the energy storage as “ultimate solution” to enable the intermittent sources for addressing utility base load needs, besides regarded it as “a storage system that has the efficiency to store in 1 day and less” may perhaps enable PV for affording 50% order of system energy [19].

Instead of selecting sufficient sized system on the basis of commercially available technologies, there are many features involved in this solar incorporating energy storage accompanied by distributed PV generation in grid-connected uses. 1.1.2 Energy storage applications in PV systems

The owner of the integrated PV solar system can get the overall advantages from the perspectives of environment, finance, and operation altogether besides utility via peak shaving and reliability applications [20]. During the supply of generated energy at one time to a load, various applications like peak shaving, load shifting, in addition to demand response are involved. The electric grid turns out to be more reliable by outage protection besides power quality control apart from any regulatory along with rate-based actions [21]. The following segment confers a few applications.

1.1.2.1 Peak shaving

This mainly helps in minimizing demand charges for a customer or diminishing loads in peak practiced through utility. Peak shaving in various PV systems greatly necessitates PV affording entire essential power beyond a definite threshold besides, if PV is inaccessible, inadequate energy storage for gap filling. Peak shave failure may lead to serious financial concerns in which customers’ rates mainly depend on peak demand in monthly basis. Consequently, reliability is a key element. For peak shaving implementation, controller in the system must be competent for power dispatching storage system whenever PV is unapproachable for satisfying load.

1.1.2.2 Load shifting

Load shifting is same as peak shaving in a technical manner; however, its application is a great benefit to consumers. The concerns purchase the power on a time-of-use basis. Many peak loads happen late in day, after passing peak for PV generation. Storage in semination with PV might be done for reducing demand for utility power throughout the day with rate times higher via storage system.

1.1.2.3 Demand response

When the electric utilities are concerned, the demand response is apt for load side management. Demand response permits the users from controlling the noncritical loads by turning it off. The critical loads can be turned on and shedding of the noncritical loads will pave a way for better load side management.

1.1.2.4 Outage protection

PV storage system’s key advantage possesses capability for offering power to consumer when power is unobtainable (i.e., for the period of outages). The difference between residence and commercial should be done so that complying with utility safety regulations aimed for back-feeding power avoidance onto transmission and distribution lines during a blackout can be done.

1.1.2.5 Power quality control

Power quality confirms voltage constancy, adjustment of phase angle, and extraneous harmonic content extraction from electric grid along with outage protection. Presently, UPS device does this function in customer side. When PV storage systems are considered, expansion for UPS can be done for better power storage.

1.1.2.6 Microgrid

Highly sustainable and reliable microgrids are attained by renewable generation and energy storage. Once operating separately from local utility microgrids incorporated with the various PV storage systems might greatly exploit PV-generated electricity for power supply to various consumers. Energy storage is vital for ensuring microgrid-stable operation through load and supply variations management besides maintaining voltage along with frequency constant. Successful microgrid integration encompasses PV storage systems to greater utility grid infrastructure which encompasses countless welfares in operation to utilities as well as consumers, nonetheless, a high system control level is necessitated, and PV storage system powerful design.

Energy storage is mainly involved in capturing energy and efficiently distributes it for upcoming use. Energy storage technologies (ESTs) deal with numerous substantial advantages: enhanced power quality stability, power supply reliability, and so on. ESTs tend to possess different classifications, which either depend on storage or based on their applications [22]. 1.1.4 Grid-connected PV systems

Solar PV technology is mainly utilized for electricity generation from solar energy. A grid-connected solar PV system is basically a solar energy panel system whose connection is done to the main power supply (“grid”). The system user utilizes electricity from both solar panel systems along with electrical grid which greatly enables user for drawing energy from grid during emergencies like on a cloudy day or throughout night. Solar PV systems classification is done into two systems such as grid-connected and stand-alone systems. Grid-connected PV systems mainly involve 99% of installed capacity in contradiction with stand-alone systems using batteries [23]. Grid-connected PV systems without battery are less expensive and necessitate lower care. The requirement of batteries is not essential in grid-connected PV. Power generated is uploaded to grid directly for transmission and distribution. In grid-connected PV systems, power conditioning unit mainly helps in DC power conversion created through PV array into AC power in accordance with utility grid voltage and power quality necessities.

1.1.5 Alternate energy storage systems and its applications

1.1.5.1 Overview of energy storage

Renewable power (PV, solar–thermal, or wind) is considered to be fundamentally intermittent in addition to fluctuations. Suppose renewable power has turn out to be a chief base-load dispatchable power source, multi-MW capacity and multi-hour duration are crucial for electricity storage systems [24]. The advanced ESSs are mainly for storing electrical energy and generation is done through renewable energy sources. These sources varies depending on the climatic conditions. On assessment basis, battery structures required for electricity storage generated from renewable energy sources are of minimal cost, have large efficiency, have extensive cycle life, have mature technology, resist high ambient temperatures, have vast power and energy volumes, and are environmentally benign.

Though there are numerous commercially electrical ESS (EESS), single storage system does not meet entire necessities for a perfect EESS. There is an appropriate range for every EESS. Storage is considered to be a vital unit for storing unstable electric energy during wind and PV power generation, which is abruptly growing new renewable energy, along with supplying unstable energy to electric power system yet once more in essential moment. The energy storage unit’s nonexistence may lead to issues such as abrupt blackout due to unstable sunlight-dependent electricity supply [25]. This storage plays a vital role in electricity storage systems for households, medium-size system for industrialized commercial use, along with extra large system for power plants and substations such as frequency regulations. Normally, ESS operation categorization is specified below:

The charging period: This is appropriate through network electrical energy, throughout off-peak intervals when electrical energy exists at lesser expenses.

The discharging period: In peak times, stored energy in an ESS is greatly utilized. Also, in this period, network electrical energy possesses greater price besides distributed generation usage is further cheap to run. On ESS application basis, reduction or even eradicating renewable distributed generation uncertainties can be attained [26].

The most widely used approaches in ESSs mainly depend on DC type which is intertwined with power electronic devices for national power grid connection. Mostly, ESS variation can be delivered pertaining to technology, location, capacity, demand, and investment expenses. Indeed, energy storage is regarded as a dominant factor in renewable sources integration, possessing a substantial part in sustaining a robust and consistent new electricity system [27]. The power fluctuations can be greatly minimized enhancing electric system flexibility and facilitating electricity generated storage and transmitting through variable renewable energy sources like wind and solar [28]. Diverse storage technologies are deployed in electric power systems which might be chemical, electrochemical, mechanical, electrical, or thermal. Energy storage capacity mainly comprises storage medium, power conversion system besides plant balance.

1.1.5.2 Technologies used in energy storage systems

ESSs offer an extensive technological methodologies array for managing power supply and creating a further resilient energy infrastructure besides carrying cost savings to utilities and customers. Various storage and storage technology types are appropriate for dissimilar applications, often estimated through the amount of time stored energy which is essential [29]. Storage is required for stabilizing and creating variable generation from solar and wind dispatchable (or “base load”), [30] EST classification is done in electrochemical storage as in batteries, electrical storage as in supercapacitors, magnetic storage, kinetic storage, and chemical storage. All these technologies pairing can be done with software that helps in controlling charge and energy discharge. Different technologies are used in ESS which are categorized as pumped storage, batteries, flywheel energy storage, superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES), regenerative fuel cell (RFC) storage, compressed air energy storage (CAES), and so on.

1.1.5.2.1 Pumped storage system

Gravity is considered to be a potent, unavoidable force contiguous at every time and one amid furthermost recognized ESTs’ pumped hydropower. Presently, it is regarded to be the greatest energy storage type which has pumped hydroelectric facilities in which utility-scale gravity storage technology is exploited for world betterment. Pumped hydroelectric facilities are considered to be a common energy storage process on grid which accounts for over 95% of storage in use currently. Throughout off-peak hours, water is pumped by turbines to an elevated reservoir through excess electricity. Whenever there is a high demand, reservoir opens allowing retained water flowing via turbines and produces electricity. This system is considered to be challenging task due to terrain requirement (an upper and water lower pool) and enormous footprint. Energy is stored in water form easing pumped hydroelectric storage in an upper reservoir, pumped from another reservoir at a lesser reservoir [31]. Throughout high electricity demand stages, power generation is done through releasing stored water via turbines in a similar way which is regarded as a traditional hydropower station. When there is lower demand, upper reservoir recharging is done through lower cost electricity from grid to pump water back to the upper reservoir. A reversible Pump-Turbine/Motor-Generator assembly performs as both pumps and turbines. Pumped storage stations are quite different from conventional hydroelectric stations in which they are net electricity consumer, because of losses sustained in pumping cycle from lower to upper reservoirs [32]. Nonetheless, these plants are usually greatly effective (round-trip efficiencies attaining >80%), and balancing load inside the entire power system is validated. Pumped storage facilities might be easy on the pocket for peak and off-peak price differentials reason and their probable for offering serious ancillary grid services.

1.1.5.2.2 Batteries

A device encompasses several electrochemical cells for stored chemical energy conversion into electrical energy is termed as battery which has a positive terminal, or cathode, and a negative terminal, or anode. Electrolytes help in permitting ions for moving amid electrodes and terminals letting current to flow out of battery for task attainment. If advanced technology is utilized in batteries, materials have greatly improved reliability, output, and modern battery systems density, and scale economies have intensely minimized associated cost. Once advanced technology is used in batteries, materials having prominently improved reliability and output will be preferred. Battery ESSs (BESS) is appropriate for individual and hybrid applications, comprising ones in amalgamation with engines, turbines, and renewable [33], which offers huge power contained by very short response time. It aids energy provider’s resource everyday power along with critical services, such as grid balancing and peak shaving, in a consistent, economical manner by traditional EMS system which enhances power supply reliability, availability, and efficiency. BESS are greatly utilized for applications such as peak shaving, frequency control and load balancing, renewable integration via ramp rate control, and energy time shift which are different energy storage types in batteries. Few are lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries, lead-acid batteries, redox flow batteries, vanadium redox flow batteries, nickel–cadmium batteries, sodium sulfur batteries, electrochemical capacitors, iron–chromium flow batteries, zinc–bromine flow batteries. The comparison of batteries for BESS is shown in Table 1.3.

1.1.5.2.3 Flywheel energy storage

A flywheel is nothing but a rotating mechanical device mainly utilized for storing rotational energy which might be called up instantly. A flywheel encompasses spinning mass in its center which is motor driven as well as spinning force initiates a device like a turbine is driven by spinning force for electricity generation slowing rotation rate. Flywheel recharging is done through motor for increasing its rotational speed another time. Flywheel technology comprises useful properties for enhancing current electric grid which has the proficiency of capturing energy from intermittent energy sources over time, as well as delivering uninterrupted power supply to grid. Flywheels have the ability for responding grid signals promptly, providing frequency regulation besides electricity eminence enhancements. Flywheel ESSs are one amid energy storage devices. They store energy mechanically in the flywheel rotor by rotating the rotor whereas chemical batteries store energy electrically. When we want to use the stored energy in the rotor, a generator is utilized for mechanical energy conversion to electrical energy. Flywheel systems are temperature insensitive; meanwhile, they operate in a vacuum containment. Therefore, the hybrid vehicle with flywheel systems might run deprived of any problem at very cold or hot areas. Also, flywheel systems might help in storing further energy per system weight in contradiction with chemical batteries. The flywheel system is the most efficient energy storage device deployed for various applications.

1.1.5.2.4 Superconducting magnetic energy storage

SMES is an innovative technology for storing electricity from grid contained in coil magnetic field encompassed of superconducting wire with near zero energy loss. SMES is considered as a grid-enabling device for storing besides discharging large power quantities almost instantly. It has proficiency of releasing high power levels contained by a cycle fraction for abrupt loss or dip in line power replacement. Power quality plays a vital part in grid reliability maintenance particularly while dealing with increasing congested power lines demand as well high renewable energy sources penetration like wind in addition solar. SMES has cryogenically cooled superconducting coil along with power conditioning system ensuing in greater consistency when compared with present power storage devices. Whenever superconducting coil charging is done ideally, current decay might not occur and magnetic energy storing will be done indeterminately.

1.1.5.2.5 Regenerative fuel cell storage

RFC operation might be accomplished as a fuel cell, consequently generating power, besides as an electrolyzer; hence, its own fuel can be generated. It is mainly regarded as an energy storage device. Power generation is mainly done by RFC systems as well as electrolytically their reactants regeneration is achieved by electrochemical cell stacks. ESSs with tremendously high specific energy (>400 Wh/kg) design is done for that utilizing lightweight pressure vessels for gases produced via reversible (unitized) RFCs. RFC acts as a key component for system power and energy component separation in contrast to battery systems. The system power output is obtained through fuel cell stack size along with system energy capacity relating hydrogen (and oxygen) storage subsystem size which are typically high-pressure gas tanks. It is greatly utilized in applications where comparatively massive electricity storage must be done, like energy storage for distant off-grid power sources, emergency or backup power generation, zero-emission vehicles, hybrid energy storage/propulsion systems for underwater vehicles, spacecraft, and high-altitude long-endurance solar rechargeable aircraft.

1.1.5.2.6 Compressed air energy storage

CAES is a process of utilizing generated stored energy for future use. Energy generated throughout low-energy demand periods (off-peak) might be released for meeting greater demand (peak load) periods at utility scale. The air compression by the compressor is greatly attained by energy from solar or wind and even electricity from thermal power plant in the course of off-peak period. In addition, same air might be used for generating electricity throughout peak hour. CAES is accomplished in underground caverns as well as abandoned mines.

1.1.5.2.7 Technological challenges for energy storage system

ESS is considered to be a potential challenge which is primarily driven by renewable and microgrid expansions in current power in infrastructure [34]. The main commercial applications of batteries are grid and electric vehicles. Large-scale storage is mainly accomplished across globally through these traditional storage systems such as Pumped Hydroelectric Storage (PHS) and Compressed Air Energy Storage (CAES) [35]. Few challenges of ESS are guaranteeing sustainability and accessing component materials, operation protection and flexibility, energy deliverability cost, international standards’ incentives for ESS investment and progress for ESS choice and implementation, weak grid and poor formed market, installation infrastructure, and maintenance necessities.

In the ESS framework, classification is accomplished for different applications like adaptable exchanging current transmission frameworks, limited scope, medium scale, enormous scope applications, framework adequacy, outflow control, top shaving, and surrendering office interests in peaking generators. Among which, few are used for medium-scale applications like pumped storage, compacted air energy stockpiling, flywheel, and superconducting attractive energy stockpiling (SMES) which has limit in MW ranges. The energy framework is the place where the components are kept in a coordinated manner to guarantee that it fulfills the purpose of generation, dispersion, control, and energy change [36]. The energy generated from the renewable sources is called renewable energy and it has various sources like sun, solar, wind, rain, tide, and geothermal. Hence, there are lot of alternatives of energy generation. Nowadays, there are a lot of advancements in energy systems, thereby enabling the monitoring of data remotely, hence, ensuring quality of service. The performance of the device along with its efficiency is calculated, and numerous analytics are predicted from it. As the renewable energy sources are numerous, the data collectors send massive amount of data bringing the big data into picture. With the help of decisions taken by the machine learning (ML) models, numerous interpretations can be made.

This interpretation is in turn helping the end user to bring a quality analysis of data. The prediction framework helps in simplifying the dependencies of data and has gained popularity in the energy sector [37, 38]. 1.1.6 Machine learning framework along with its tools and types

1.1.6.1 Basics of AI

Artificial intelligence (AI) is a group or a cluster of techniques which gives an attempt to mimic human intelligence, nature, and behavior. It was first coined by John McCarthy through a research project on AI at Dartmouth in the year 1956. Hence, AI is a collection of theories, ideas, and techniques, which includes logics, probabilities, and computational techniques and imitates or resembles the human cognitive abilities. Applications of AI are numerous.

They are used in data mining, diagnosing of disease, recognizing speech, predictive analysis, smart email categories, plagiarism checkers, robot readers, fraud preventions, giving recommendations, smart personal assistants, playing chess, and so on. There are a lot of definitions of AI according to many scientists as represented in Table 1.4.

Table 1.4:Overview on AI according to the scientists view.

Year Scientists view About AI
1978 Bellman AI is when the activities associate with human thinking abilities like decision making, learning, and problem solving
1981 A. Barr and E.A. Feigenbaum A system that exhibits human behavior like understanding concepts, understanding language, reasoning, learning, and solving problems
1990 Schalkoff Reproducing intelligence in terms of computational process
1990 Kurzweil Functions that require intelligence when it is operated by humans
1991 Rich and Knight Study of making the computers do things
1993 Luger and Stubblefield Automation and intelligent behavior
1995 Dean.et.al A study of computer program that behaves intelligently
1998 Nilsson Writing computer programs, solving mathematics, understanding languages, and driving an automobile requires intelligence which is an AI

On the whole, AI is mimicking the behavior of humans in order to perform and entertain the human beings, instruct the people, reveal useful information, and do activities even better than human beings. To check whether the computer is thinking like a human or not, the Turing test is carried out. Alan Turing proposed a methodology where there are two opponents: human and machine that acts like a human. The type of conversation is a text-only channel and the evaluator will check for it. The evaluator if fails to reliably understand the difference between the machine and human, the machine has passed the test. In this way, the machines are analyzed whether they are following AI standard or not. Figures 1.2 and 1.3 show the operation of the machine and AI machine.

A machine will get the input and transform into the desired output depending on the circuits and sensors inbuilt in the machines. An AI machine will get the input and perform analysis on the data, come with the predicted output, and check whether the predicted output goes well with the actual output. The dataset is split into trained and test, and analysis is made from the data. If the new data enters into the dataset, it can be automatically added to the test data or train data with the help of codes. The AI has very levels depending on the way in which the AI competes with the human behavior. The narrow AI is where the machine performs tasks better than human beings. The general AI can be defined as the state where the accuracy level of human and the machine is the same. The strong AI is when the machines lead the human-level accuracy.

AI is a computer that tries to exhibit human-like properties. It tries to mimic the human behavior. The ML is a subset of AI which trains the machine so as to mimic human behavior. The training can be given by the humans or it can be trained by itself too. The programmers can give examples and train the machine and once the training is over, the machine starts to learn by itself which is possible. Deep learning (DL) is the subset of ML wherein the understanding about the source is made even more possible as shown in Figure 1.4. Let us consider an example of image recognition; the DL has various layers in it to understand the image and to come out with the predicted outcome.

1.1.6.2 Why machine learning?

The main reason to go for ML is because it has improved healthcare and agriculture field, eliminates the need to perform tedious task, reduces the accidents by decreasing the complications related to traffic, provides digital consultation, reduces the human error, and so on. The ML algorithms have been invented so long ago, and are gaining massive popularity nowadays because of the data. The huge amount of data received nowadays is massive that the ML tools give a very good prediction which was not the case in those days. The cost of storage and the cost of computing are declining nowadays, paving a way for ML to come in a big picture. More data can be stored and processed in recent times leading to more prediction. The data can be structured and semistructured or unstructured depending on the application.

The log files, tweets, blogs, audio, and videos are all good examples of semistructured or unstructured data. Lot of things are connected to Internet, wherein the survey studies tell that there are more Internet connected devices than the world population is considered. Nowadays, data scientists describe the data and use yotta bytes, and in future, brontobyte will be the measurement values. People are expecting the machine to behave like humans, thereby demanding cognitive computing. The devices and systems are becoming smarter and the expectations of the human beings are becoming huge day and day.

Wearable healthcare and fitness trackers, smart agriculture, connected vehicles, weather forecasting, smart cities, and tele medicine smart surveillance are all indeed a boon to the human beings. All the predictions and real-time analytics are possible with ML. The dataset is split into train data and test data, and the ML models are applied to it.

1.1.6.3 Types of machine learning models

The machine needs to undergo three stages, which include data storage and abstraction, generalization, and evaluation of data. The data is stored and translated into the same in a broader way in data storage and abstraction stage. The knowledge interpretation of data takes place in generalization, and the feedback is provided to improve the data learnt in the later stage. There are three classifications of ML models as shown in Figure 1.5.

The supervised learning platform learns itself by the labeled data. This data can be used for accurate mapping between the input and output. The algorithms under supervised learning can identify the features exactly and hence prediction can be made accordingly. When two variables are considered, it can easily predict the relationship between them and an outcome is obtained. The facial recognition, signature recognition, predicting house prices, stock prices prediction, discovery of customers, and so on are good examples of supervised learning. It is of two types as shown in Figure 1.6.

The classification models under supervised learning are used when the output is a binary value. The answer when it is True or False, Pass or Fail, this model is used. The lazy learners in classification model will wait for the testing data to arrive. The eager learners will try to learn itself with the training data and will try to come out with the predictions. The most important classification algorithms are discussed. Logistic regression will depend on the one, two, or more independent variables and come to a classified output. The k-nearest neighbor algorithm will look into the nearest neighbor and try to label them. K is the value which is the number of neighbors that the algorithm checks. Naive Bayes classifier predicts the output depending on the probability of the features. Even if the features are dependent to each other, the probability is calculated separately. Stochastic gradient descent updates the training data when the derivative is calculated. Decision tree will have a root node and classification is done on the top-down method where the data is divided into small structures for accurate prediction of values. Larger decision trees are combined together to form a random forest. It is a metaseparator that ensembles all the decision trees in it. A margin and a hyperplane are created in the support vector machine (SVM), and when new points arise it looks into place where it needs to be located. Some algorithms along with the advantages, drawbacks and use cases are discussed in Table 1.5.

Once the trained and test data are subjected to the ML models, the following three values appear in the classification report: accuracy, F1 score, and precision and recall. Accuracy is the ratio of correctly predicted values to the total values which were observed. TP is the number of positive predictions. TN is the number of negative predictions. Recall the fraction of relevant case among the total instances. The average value of recall and precision value is known as F1 score. The curve drawn between TP and FP is called the ROC curve. Hence, accuracy of the model is known with the help of ROC curve. The unsupervised learning works on the unlabeled data. The reinforcement learning is a process where the machine is exposed to data and understands it on a trial-and-error basis. It learns itself from the past experience and tries to come out with the best solution for it. There are many algorithms under the above-listed models. The models may overlap sometimes, and hence a lot of training of data are required to come out with the best model for the problem statement. There are various steps required to choose the best algorithm required for the user application. The dataset needs to be understood by understanding the features, and the dataset is split into train and test data. The models are trained and evaluated, and the best classifier is chosen as shown in Figure 1.7.

Every layer has an activation function in it which helps in processing of data. The data is gone through each layer, utilizing the values from the previous layers. 1.1.8 Machine learning in renewable energy

An ML model finds a lot of applications in energy systems. There are numerous parameters which need to be measured in solar panels, especially with respect to ESS in concern. The forecasting of solar power generation, prediction of energy demand, forecasting for daily solar radiation and wind speed, prediction of hourly global radiation, predicting power output of solar system, hourly global solar radiation prediction, forecasting in PV generation of power, prediction of average globe ration, analyzing the PV electrical characteristics, estimating the PV system module temperature, short-term forecasting of loads in microgrid are some of the few. The energy storage can either make use of the battery, heat, or pumped hydroelectric storage in general. The modeling and prediction are easier when the energy systems are integrated with the ML models. There are eight frequently used methodologies when the integration between the ML models along with the energy system takes place. They are artificial neural network (ANN), MLP, decision trees, DL, ensembles, wavelet neural network, and ANN-based fuzzy and advanced hybrid ML models [40]. The procedure to implement Machine Learning in renewable energy sector is shown in Figure 1.11.

In the first stage, the problem is identified by analyzing the various renewable sources of energy. Stage 2 is to find which data needs to be monitored for efficient scheduling of loads. Stage 3 is to make a real-time analysis and application for a smartphone so as to make the portability easier. Stage 4 involves bringing solution for scheduling of loads by monitoring the sources if possible (solar panels in case of solar energy). Condition-based monitoring is cost-effective by looking into cost–benefit analysis [41] as shown in Figure 1.12.

1.1.8.1 Solar parameter estimation

1.1.8.1.1 Data acquisition from the solar panel

Similar cells are connected together to form modules. For a nominal voltage charging of 12 V, a maximum of 36 cells are needed. About 30 mA/cm2 is the maximum current that can be delivered. If the panel is working under standard test conditions with no complications on damaged cell, shading, and others, then the expected outcome will help in prediction of loads and forecasting. The bypass diodes and blocking diodes should help in reducing the losses ensuring uniform production of units. The panel has been maintained properly ensuring no parts are mechanically corroded and are free from debris. The electrical checks have been carried out often assuring that the wiring is not damaged. The solar panels have to overcome optical losses, recombination losses, top contact design losses, grid spacing losses, and others to ensure the optimum output under Standard Test Conditions. The top contact coverage, antireflection coatings, and surface texturing can reduce the optical losses. The shading losses, resistive losses, and contact losses will indirectly affect the output units being generated. Hence, before the process of data acquisition, these criteria have been considered. In case solar energy is preferred, the panels need to be maintained properly for smooth and efficient operation of loads. The maintenance of panels will ensure that it is operated safely and efficiently. The solar panel maintenance is shown in Figure 1.13.

Maintenance can be classified into predictive and corrective depending on the usage. The condition of the panels along with their frequency of arrival of data can be predicted very easily in preventive maintenance leading to prediction. The break down is analyzed in corrective maintenance. The monitoring system of the solar panels will give an overall idea on the performance of the panels. The information about the power levels can be collected and used for further analytics. The units generated and the energy consumption can be calculated easily. The data are acquired by the acquisition module fitted in the source which in turn send the value to the next stage of processing as shown in Figure 1.14.

The number of units generated along with the energy consumption can be visualized using the mobile phones. Historical data can also be measured with the help of IoT and ML. The monitoring software gives an idea on the weather-based performance, thereby enabling the comparison of weather conditions along with the load conditions leading to more precise load forecasting and load scheduling. Hence, the overall picture of analyzing the data with respect to the source will vary. When solar panels are considered numerous parameters like system status, energy generation, temperature of panel, temperature of air, global irradiance, POA irradiance, wind speed, total AC power, and total DC power can be measured accurately with the help of sensors fitted in the solar panels. Big data are used to monitor the data at large scale. Dashboard reports will give an understanding of the solar plant performance. Figure 1.15 gives an overall idea on the maintenance of the panel. The influencing factors of PV are analyzed, and entropies are considered for better prediction [40].

1.1.8.1.2 Literature survey on ML models with solar power generation and forecasting of loads

The output is completely dependent on the parameter selection of the PV modules. There are lot of parameters present in solar module which will affect the lifetime and efficiency if wrongly chosen. The maximum power, its density, fill factor, and open-circuit voltage have a lot of possibilities to decrease the cell performance. The open circuit is the maximum voltage generating condition at zero current. It depends on the generation of photo current which represents the open-circuit voltage. kB represents the Boltzmann constant, with q representing the charge of the electron, J0 indicating the current density at saturation stage, and Mph talking about the photo current density. The conversion efficiency is another important parameter under consideration. The ratio of maximum power to the ratio of incident light determines the conversion efficiency. Hence, Voc, Isc, FF, Vmp, Imp, and area under radiance are typical characteristics of the solar cell. With respect to the number of solar cells designed, the above-mentioned parameters are estimated and designed.

The dataset is obtained by considering all these values. The dataset is divided into validation data and test data, and evaluation is made by undergoing cross-fold validation technologies. When the values are predicted, the following factors have to be considered without neglecting. The blocking diode causes the loss of 0.6 V. If the light intensity reduces, it might again lead to losses. So, all these factors have to be considered for efficient dataset. Metaheuristics helps in estimating the parameters properly enhancing the prediction. The new set of parameters will be used for each iteration in the ML models. These models estimate the SOC along with SOH, Li-ion batteries capacity, Li-ion batteries SOC, online SOH, accuracy with less than 1% of error, charging position, idling position, and discharging position analysis.

Hence, the lifetime of batteries can be estimated and predicted easily as the SOH and SOC is known to us. Table 1.12 gives the analysis of the model with the result. The depth of discharge indicating the amount discharged from the fully charged battery is also considered. The shallow cycle and deep cycle batteries are meant to give usage of power supply till 25% and 50% of discharging, respectively. These processes are done before recharging. The remaining useful time in a battery gives better accuracy but it is difficult to predict it. Predicting the remaining useful time of a battery can be done by health indicator and GPR model application. When the charging process is carried out with constant voltage and constant current, the features are extracted from the health indicator with good modeling, and benefits are numerous as the accuracy is of high prediction. For fusion of algorithms with filters, a complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition methodology is a most promising technique present to enhance the predicted lifetime of the batteries. Fuel cells are another storage method in ESSs which will convert the chemical energy into electricity. Electrochemical process is followed. The optimized design of fuel cells can be done once the losses pertaining to it are understood. This will enact the prediction in a smooth manner. Polymer electrolyte membrane is a type of fuel cell that has a lot of applications in stationary and portable side. These cells have membrane electrode assemblies. A methodology regularizing the particle filter incorporating the least square SVM (LSSVM) is used to forecast the voltage change pattern [77]. LSTM model can also be used in predicting the remaining useful life of the fuel cell. Stacked sparse autoencoder is added with deep neural network (DNN) to predict the fault of fuel cells. The unlabeled data are fine-tuned and mapping is done [78]. LSSVM is used in most of the application of ESSs of fuel cells where the dataset is split into trained model and test model. The input vector and trained model are trained with respect to time in the initial stage, and compared with the test dataset. The sliding window enacts the output as well. To brief, the features are extracted and fine tuned, sparse autoencoder is stacked, the measurement matrix is done with online data and collected data from the system, and prediction is performed. These ML techniques help in proper designing of the fuel cell. A hybrid storage energy system is a combination of one or more storage systems. The time series curve is a combination of annual record with respect to generation, production, and weather condition. DNN combined with time series data is suitable for hybrid ESSs. These data help in making the dataset in a good fashion enabling unified architecture across the network. The interoperability standards have been ensured as the devices are numerous, and this heterogeneous network will cause a lot of security issues. Hence, the agent system in reinforcement learning outperforms the work and enables uniform interface between the client and server. The agent behaves in the uncertain environment and works accordingly. The environment and the actions are learnt well by the agent by means of repeated learning and the agent receives awards if performed well. With the help of rewards further, process is moved forward. If there are no rewards, the process is again revised and studied again. This feedforwarding will make the agents learn the environment in a even more better manner. The speed and user friendliness of various ML models are considered, and the following analysis is made as shown in Figures 1.17 and 1.18 [38].

The complexity and the accuracy are analyzed for various ML models. The DL and ensemble techniques are complex, and the other methodologies like MLP, decision trees, ANFIS, and hybrids are reasonably complex when compared to SVM and other techniques.

1.1.9 Conclusions

The main issues in global warming are giving rise to renewable energy. Hence, prediction of renewable energy has become a big area of research to work on. When the environmental conditions are complex and the flexibility of loads is not uniform, there is requirement of machine learning model in the renewable energy sector to inculcate more prediction in the data. The data have to be analyzed carefully removing the noises, and proper processing of data ensures correct prediction. The ML models with respect to solar ESS predictions is analyzed in this chapter. When the ML models are analyzed with respect to speed and user friendliness, the following analysis is made. The MLP, ensemble, ANFIS, and hybrid speed are reasonably high when compared with SVM and other techniques. When the relative study analysis of ML models in energy systems with respect to user friendliness is considered, the hybrid model stands relatively high and ELM model stands reasonably high. ANN, SVM, DT, Ensemble and WNN has low user friendliness and the models like MLP, DL and ANFIS has reasonable friendliness for the ML models in energy systems. The solar radiation can be forecasted with various ML models, and the performance can be predicted. Hence, ML has solved a range of issues in the ESSs by understanding their state, diagnosing the fault and predicting their lifetime. Algorithms combine multiply to provide a unified approach to the dataset. Linear regression algorithms are suitable for dataset, the nonlinearity in dataset may pose a trouble with its complex featurisms, and SVR has lot of advantages on its nonlinearity and has better accuracy. In future, algorithms and models in ML can be further optimized to meet the requirements of ESS. Data preprocessing, data munging, and data translation can be carried out efficiently to predict the exact behavior of modules. Failure detection in nanoscale and macroscale fabrication also needs to be considered in future research work. More research can be focused on smart ESS, where IoT can be combined with the ML [89] for obtaining the dataset. The quality of service in application-layer protocols of IoT will enhance the user friendliness and improve the quality outcome. The heterogeneous networks can be connected together with standardization, and future implications can be more on the industrial IoT too. The security is the major concern when such an integration is enabled and hence proper firewalls and VPN can help in protecting the data. Authorization, access control, and authentication methodologies can be an additional protection to the data. Hence, future trends are more on smart energy systems incorporating IoT with ML.

2 Power control of modified type III DFIG-based wind turbine system using four-mode type I fuzzy logic controller

Bibhu Prasad Ganthia
School of Electrical Engineering, KIIT Deemed to be University, Bhubaneswar
Subrat Kumar Barik
School of Electrical Engineering, KIIT Deemed to be University, Bhubaneswar
Byamakesh Nayak
School of Electrical Engineering, KIIT Deemed to be University, Bhubaneswar

Abstract

This chapter is devoted to the implementation of advanced controlled techniques to enhance the generation in wind energy system. Here, in this chapter, various modified fuzzy logic controllers are used to regulate the active power (P) and reactive power (Q) under transient conditions. The transient or the fault analysis is done with three-phase fault applied to the grid-integrated wind energy system. Here, in this chapter, modified rotor-based type III wind turbine system is implemented. Doubly fed induction generator is used in type III wind turbine system as the operating generator. Various modes of fuzzy logic structures are used as controllers in addition to the conventional PI controller. This adaptive controller is able to offer quicker settling time and faster response toward the transients occurred due to rapid change in wind speed or any other criteria for causing faults. All techniques are applied in the wind turbine design to get better result in comparison to other fuzzy logic controllers. Here, MATLAB is used for simulink design of the system and validated using real-time software TYPHOON HIL. The main motive is to validate that the modified type III wind turbine system can give efficient result using adaptive techniques to control active and reactive power. This chapter can be helpful for the researchers to analyze their works reference with these research findings.

Keywords: wind energy, type III wind turbine, FLC type I, power analysis, active power, reactive power, power smoothing,

2.1 Introduction

Wind energy as a renewable source of energy is now such a demand for all power sectors because of the clean and free availability [1, 2]. For balancing the power demand, it can play a valuable role to enhance the efficiency of the energy for both commercial and domestic utilities [3, 4, 5]. The best part of this source of energy is that there is no hazardous emission of harmful gases from it which cause environmental pollution [6, 7, 8]. Hence, it is used as a perfect source of energy and can fulfill our energy demand [9, 10]. We need balance and stable power system with full control to achieve high output [11]. Renewable sources nowadays play a vital role to balance out the huge power GTD system. Now we produce 15 to 20 million MW power from renewable sources, and wind is the most economic source of power generation. This can be used as a standalone mode as well as grid integrated for smoothing the power demands [12]. Technical wind turbine system needs both mechanical and electrical components for full control over the generation, transmission, and distribution of power. Initially, we are using doubly fed induction generators (DFIGs) without any control mechanism which causes losses due to sudden changes in wind speed as these are designed for fixed speed mode of operation [13]. Later on, we develop type III wind turbine system which uses DFIGs with full control over speed and power generations. These are designed with rotor side and grid side converter based on maximum power point tracking abilities. Then type IV PMSG is used but the cost is so high, and these mechanisms are less used in the world. In our country India, type III DFIGs are used in maximum and play efficient power generations in both stand-alone and grid-connected mode. But the controller to the rotor side and grid side should be more precise, and faster responsive techniques should be implemented. Many researchers are using adaptive techniques like genetic algorithms, artificial intelligence, and metaheuristic controllers for fault analysis during transients [14]. Fuzzy logic controller (FLC) is also a good sign of control technique that can be implemented to give faster response toward the transients. As the wind energy system needs constant wind speed for the quality power generation, the wind speed should maintain balanced under low and high speed [15, 16]. Unpredictable flow of wind can cause damage to the system, so the controller for the rotor side and grid side should be properly examined and implemented [17].

Here, in this chapter, four modes of fuzzy logic rule bases are used to fully control the active and reactive power during rapid change in wind speed under transients. Four different fuzzy logic rules and adaptive-type controller are used here with the conventional PI controller for steady-state and transient analysis. As DFIGs are best for variable wind speed operations, this chapter devoted to modify the rotor side gear system and called it as modified rotor system-based type III wind turbines. The PWM-based converter controller is used to reduce the harmonics during transients and capacitor bank installed to reduce the switching losses. The modified rotor is used for both sub-synchronous mode and super-synchronous modes of operations. Operation of both modes is effective for low-speed and high-speed operations of wind speed. Rotor side converter and stator side converter are individually controlled by fuzzy logic control structures, and the power generation under transients is studied. For power smoothing, this technique is helpful for variable wind speeds. This adaptive control technique is helpful for smoothing the output power and maintains the stability under sudden faults. The pitch angle, the maximum power point tracking, the RSC and GSC operated using these adaptive techniques for stable power generation process [18]. This system is validated using a real-time software TYPHOON HIL 402. The validation results are compared with the simulink results, and a comparative analysis is done in the end.

2.2 Wind energy conversion systems

Sunlight is the reason of atmospheric heating which causes the wind to flow. In hot and cold regions due to pressure gradients, the wind flows from higher pressure region to lower. This process is regular and unbalanced in between low and high speeds. The kinetic energy of the wind pressure causes the wind to flow at seashore more than that of offshore. So maximum wind energy generating stations are located nearer to the seashore areas. Figure 2.1 depicted the detailed block diagram of a grid-connected wind energy system. Here, the model can be categorized into four componential areas; first is aerodynamic control which has wind flow, wind turbine blades and a hub which interconnected with turbine blades. Second part is mechanical assembled system having gearbox and mechanical coupler with the shaft. Third one is electrical converter models having rotor side and grid side converter power electronics components [19, 20]. The last one is the grid interface which is associated with the wind energy system under grid integrations. For stand-alone mode and islanded mode of operation, the wind system is not connected to the grid. The wind flow causes the blade to rotate under low speed and high speed which develop mechanical motion inside the turbine, and gear box helps to fasten the speed of the rotor for a single rotation of blades [21, 22].

The control schemes are also associated in each block for efficient output from the wind energy. The pitch angle controller controls the movement of the blades and activates itself under low speed and overspeed of wind. The wind turbulence and wind flow make the blades rotate and the mechanical system inside the hub helps to rotate the wind turbine. This mechanical effect generates emf inside the synchronous generator that is used inside the system. The converter controls are categorized into two parts. First one is the rotor side controller and second one is the grid side controller. DFIGs can be very much useful for variable speed of operations. Simple PWM or back-to-back converter model can be used to reduce the transients and can reduce the harmonics by a capacitor bank connected parallel. The grid interface is connected directly to the grid side converter with transmission line parameters. See Figure 2.1.

The wind turbine system using this type III DFIGs can get maximum power of up to 30% enhancement than that of the uncontrolled type III DFIGs or partial controllers. Fixed speed and variable speed control techniques for the wind energy generation are outdated, so now the fully controlled wind turbine systems are used worldwide. Permanent magnet-based synchronous generators as type IV are also coming into account for the generations of wind energy but due to high cost it is little bit less useful than that of type III [10]. For controlling torque and speed this DFIGs are efficient. The maintenance is required in DFIG based systems but in type IV less maintenance is required. The active and reactive power control can be done using this proposed model and studied in this chapter.

2.3 DFIG-based type III wind turbine systems

Type III wind turbine uses DFIGs for generating power with synchronous speed of rotations. Figure 2.2 illustrates the power smoothing of (P) active power and (Q) reactive power control using the proposed technique described in next section. These models possess P control and Q control assemblers which are directly connected to the control model to reduce the errors that arise during transient operations. The architecture of the model is based on dq reference frame, and under transient it acts as a rotational frame for effective control action [23]:

(2.1)Vds = Rsids + dΨds/dt − ωdqsΨds
(2.2)Vqs = Rsiqs + dΨ qs/dt + ωdqsΨ qs
(2.3)Vdr = Rridr + dΨ dr/dt − ωdqrΨ qr
(2.4)Vqr = Rriqr + dΨ qr/dt + ωdqrΨ dr
(2.5)Ψ ds = Lssids + Lmidr
(2.6)Ψ qs = Lssiqs + Lmiqr
(2.7)Ψ dr = Lmids + Lrridr
(2.8)Ψ qr = Lmiqs + Lrriqr
(2.9)(Torque) Tm = 1.5pLm(iqsidr − idsiqr) = 1.5p(Ψ dsiqs − Ψ qsids)

The rotational speed of the wind turbine and the electromagnetic torque produced from the above model is represented using the above mathematical equations [24]. The mathematical modeling comprises flux, torque, direct and quadrature axes resistive loads and inductive loads, angular velocity, mutual inductances, and self-inductances symbolizing the MATLAB frame design [25, 26].

The moment of inertia-based electromagnetic torque equation is presented as follows:

(2.10)$T_{m} - T_{e} = \frac{J}{P}\frac{dw_{r}}{dt}$

Mechanical torque, electrical torque, input to the DFIGs presented in the above equation [27, 28, 29]. The moment of inertia motion reference with the power fluctuations characterized the membership function for the fuzzy rules. This makes the active and reactive power control indirectly for power smoothing. This proposed model is active, and faster responsive for both steady saturated mode and transient mode. The transient due to sudden speed change can be effectively noted from this model. In further section, the use of various modes of techniques for the adaptive controller is described and discussed [30, 31].

2.4 Type I FLC control strategies of grid-connected WECS

Active power and reactive power control for power smoothing in the grid-integrated wind energy system is the major factor to get efficient output. Conventional controllers are common nowadays. But its effectiveness toward the settling of fault is always in demand. So adaptive controllers are taken into account, as both conventional and other controllers are simultaneously helpful for power smoothing for integrated systems [32, 33]. Hence, FLC takes place as an adaptive controller with this conventional. Here, in this chapter, PI is taken as a conventional controller with multiplexed FLC to achieve the target. Four different types of modes are designed in this chapter for controlling active and reactive power [34]. Type I fuzzy rule logic controller with PI controller is used in both rotor side and grid side for controlling the stator voltage which directly controls the power generated from the wind energy system. Stator voltage-oriented control technique is used to control the voltage under transients caused by sudden changes in the wind speed. Various parameters are considered here to maintain the power quality. During grid integration, the FLC and PI simultaneously control the voltage when it goes beyond the reference. Figure 2.3 illustrates the phasor diagram of the stator voltage control for normal and transient operations [35]. The proposed technique is helpful for both steady-state and transient analyses. Here in this chapter transient analysis is done and validated using HIL real-time software. Various modes of operations are presented with controlled parameters using Mamdani type I fuzzy rules [36].

The rotating frame of reference for the stator voltage-oriented control technique is represented in Figure 2.3. Taking d and q reference frames and the voltages associated with axes are taken as main parameters. These parameters are controlled and assigned using fuzzy rules [37]. The frame of rotation depends on the wind speed and Gaussian wind speed model taken for wind speed generations for the model. By adopting the d and q reference voltages, the proposed techniques control the active and reactive powers under transients. The pulsations in the input parameters are controlled using adaptive PI-T1FLC. Four different modes are explained below with detailed block diagrams. Figure 2.4 illustrates the type I FLC associated with member function for the power control with stator d and q voltages [38].

Figure 2.4 is based on rules which are defined by the stator voltages. The interface system is taken as a controlling block for the d and q references frame voltages. The fuzzification done reference with the wind speed and the input to the fuzzy system is active and reactive power reference with d and Q voltages. The membership function with rules limits the errors due to the transients and enhances the power from the grids [39, 40].

Mode 1

Figure 2.5 represents the derivative adaptive controller with fuzzy rules for controlling the active and reactive powers. This model enhances the power quality by reducing the error by derivation. The fuzzy rules limit the error and minimize the transients due to abrupt change in stator voltage due to wind speed. The set point and the reference value errors can be predictable for power quality and its stability. Due to poor slow process of this mode 1 derivative, controller for steady-state and transient operation of this model is not so useful. The outputs are presented in results section.

Mode 2

The integral controller is not used alone, so FLC associated with this produces saturated output. But the problem in this type of model shown in Figure 2.6 is under transients and is limited to the output. It cannot go beyond the saturation limit during the fault arises due to wind speed variations. Due to slow transient operation, this mode 2 is also not used much for power smoothing.

Mode 3

Figure 2.7 illustrates the PI control action with adding derivative controller to operate under transients. We can get faster response from this adaptive control technique. This system brings the transients to steady state faster than that of P-FLC and D-FLC. We can achieve better settling time in mode 3 than that of control techniques in modes 1 and 2. The active and reactive powers are controlled to be slow when we consider the stability point of view. Marginal errors can be detected and cause ambiguity in the system during overspeed conditions. Results are comparing in the proceeding chapters.

Mode 4

The conventional controller PI associated with another integral controller combining method achieves faster response for both under speed and overspeed. Integral controller with PI and fuzzy rule-based system stops the fluctuations and fastens the settling time. The active (P) power and reactive (Q) powers can be controlled by minimizing the overshoot and fasten the settling time under fault conditions. The block diagram presented in Figure 2.8 highlights the proposed technique for control operations. This technique is useful for both steady-state and transient operations using rule-based membership function for optimizing the powers. The membership (triangular) function uses fuzzy rules shown in Figure 2.9 for the power smoothing.

2.5 Simulink results

The mathematical model is designed using MATLAB simulink. Here type III wind turbine system is used, where DFIG is implemented for variable wind speed operations. For both rotor side and grid side control, type I FLC with above four modes of operations are carried out. The gain values are taken according to the specific demand of the system for both steady (saturation) and transient operation. Comparing all techniques, the proposed controller mode IV type I PII FLC shows better response during faults. For all techniques, active and reactive powers are considered, and under transient conditions the parameters are studied and the basic model is shown in Figure 2.10.

The model is taken 1.5 MW wind turbine system as rated generating capacity. Rated cut in and cut out speeds for the model are taken as 4 and 12 m/s, respectively. The maximum voltage for the operation is taken as 690 V. The maximum wind speed is taken as 2,500 rpm with minimum of 1,500 rpm. DC link is used to maintain the balance between the RSC and GSC to reduce harmonics. The capacitor is used as a filter for the model as the system is used under transient conditions. The wind turbine modeling and the basic outputs are shown in Figures 2.11–2.24. In this model of simulink operation, transient conditions are taken.

The simulink results are shown in Figures 2.11–2.24.

2.5.2 Mamdani type I fuzzy logic control technique (degree of convergence)

The proposed adaptive technique using controller of mode 4 type I fuzzy logic uses triangular Gaussian membership function interfaced with the rules of the active and reactive power. The rules are associated with the control parameters like voltage, wind speed, and environmental aspects like dusts and ice blocks. For the Gaussian membership function, both input and output are considered to optimize the error and to improve the transient stability.

The simulation results from Figures 2.37–2.41 represent the convergence characteristics of the Gaussian function using PII mode 4 type I basic FLC. The triangular membership function considerably optimizes the convergence of the active power, reactive power, electromagnetic torque, and speed of the wind turbine power generation system under transients.

2.7 Conclusion

Wind energy is most abundant and freely available without hazardous emission during power generations. So enhancing this renewable source using advanced techniques can accelerate the power producing capabilities by maintaining the stability of our modern power system. This chapter is helpful for the recent researchers to know the modification in type II wind turbine system can reduce the cost for maintenance and damages during faults. The proposed technique mode 4 type I fuzzy logic controller can be a good choice for the wind energy generation firms for both stand-alone and grid-integrated modes. For power smoothing, this proposed technique is one of the active and efficient choices. Active and reactive power control using the proposed technique is presented in this chapter. Validating the MATLAB model with advanced and latest real-time software (TYPHOON HIL) also helps the current researchers to gain knowledge to work with type II interval-type controller technique. For linear and nonlinear operations, this technique will also be very helpful. The proposed technique used in the modified rotor-based type III wind turbine system under grid integration is effectively used for enhancing our modern power system by maintaining the stability of it.
